pageCache.text:
Meet the Senior Team
Mr Richard Woolley BA (Hons), MA (Ed), QTS, AST, NPQH Headteacher
Mr Woolley is a values-led education leader with over 25 years’ experience in schools, including more than 17 years in senior leadership roles across mainstream, Church of England and specialist autism and SEMH settings. Throughout his career, he has led schools and provisions where young people with complex needs feel safe, supported and able to achieve their very best. His approach combines high expectations with excellent safeguarding, trauma-informed practice and an ambitious, engaging curriculum, creating calm and nurturing environments in which students thrive.
Mr Woolley is proud to lead Sunnydown School and shares its commitment to helping students grow in confidence, develop independence and prepare for life beyond school. He believes that when students are known and valued, they flourish, and he works closely with staff, families and governors to ensure that every young person at Sunnydown feels supported, challenged and celebrated as part of the school community.
Mr Jez Lord BSc (Hons), PGCE Deputy Head
Mr Lord began his teaching career in Physical Education before becoming a Head of Sixth Form in Middlesex. He joined Sunnydown School in 2011 and has since dedicated over 15 years to supporting young people with special educational needs. Combined with 12 years of pastoral leadership in mainstream education, he brings a wealth of experience in helping students thrive both academically and personally.
Mr Lord is passionate about supporting young people as they navigate the opportunities and challenges of adolescence. He is committed to helping students develop confidence, resilience and independence, while recognising and celebrating the strengths that neurodiversity brings.
Mrs Jo Wermig M.Ed, BA (Hons), PGCE, NASENCO Deputy Head
Mrs Wermig joined Sunnydown School in the summer term of 2022. Having lived locally for most of her life and taught across London and Surrey, she brings a breadth of experience from both single-sex and mixed school settings. As a mother of four sons, she offers a deep understanding of the developmental and pastoral needs of young people.
With over 25 years of teaching experience across primary and secondary phases, including more than 15 years in senior leadership and previous headship roles, she has developed a strong commitment to supporting pupils with special educational needs. Her passion for nurturing each individual and responding to a wide range of learning differences has led her to Sunnydown, where she is proud to be part of a vibrant community and to support the learning journeys of all students.
Mr Ben Wright Assistant Headteacher
Mr Wright joined Sunnydown School in 2006 as a Residential Care Officer and has demonstrated exceptional commitment to the school community over nearly two decades. He began his teaching career at Sunnydown in 2010, teaching Physical Education and mathematics, and quickly established himself as a dedicated and highly valued member of staff.
In 2015, he became Key Stage 4 Coordinator, taking on responsibility for careers education alongside pastoral care and behaviour, where he played a key role in supporting students’ personal development and preparing them for life beyond school. In September 2024, he joined the Senior Leadership Team as Assistant Headteacher, continuing to lead on careers and behaviour.
Mr Wright’s long-standing service reflects his deep understanding of the school, its values and its pupils. His consistency, loyalty and genuine care for young people have made a lasting impact, and he is widely respected for the strong relationships he builds and the positive difference he makes to students’ lives.
Mrs Helen Gower School Business Manager
Mrs Gower joined Sunnydown School in 2019 and became School Business Manager in November 2021. She brings extensive experience in finance and risk management, having spent 14 years working within the banking and financial institutions sector as an Associate Director of Credit and Senior Analyst.
She is passionate about supporting the effective and efficient running of the school. Outside of work, she enjoys spending time with family and friends, watching films and baking, with a particular speciality in lemon drizzle cake.

Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Sunnydown School
At Sunnydown, we believe that every student matters, every student belongs and every student is supported to succeed. These principles sit at the heart of everything we do and shape the caring, ambitious and inclusive community we are proud to be.
We understand that every young person’s journey is different. Many of our students join us needing renewed confidence in themselves, in education and in their future. Our role is to provide the support, consistency and encouragement that allows every student to feel safe, valued and ready to achieve success in ways that are meaningful to them.
Relationships are central to life at Sunnydown. We know that students thrive when they are understood, respected and supported by adults who genuinely care about them. Our staff work tirelessly to create an environment where students feel a strong sense of belonging, develop resilience and grow in confidence both academically and personally.
Our curriculum is designed to prepare students not only for qualifications, but for life beyond school. Alongside strong academic foundations, we place great importance on personal development, communication, independence and preparation for adulthood. Through practical learning opportunities, enrichment experiences and our Friday Curriculum, students are encouraged to apply their learning in real-world contexts, discover their strengths and develop aspirations for the future.
We are proud of the broad opportunities available to our students. Whether through sport, outdoor learning, leadership opportunities, college partnerships, vocational pathways or creative experiences, we want every young person to find areas where they can succeed, contribute and grow.
Pastoral care is woven through every aspect of school life.
We recognise the importance of supporting students emotionally as well as academically, ensuring that they feel secure, listened to and able to overcome challenges positively. Our values of belonging, respect, resilience and aspiration are visible throughout the school and underpin the culture we build together every day.
At Sunnydown, we are committed to helping every student leave us with the confidence, qualifications, life skills and self-belief needed for their next stage in education, employment and adult life. We are incredibly proud of our students and the progress they make during their time with us.
Thank you for visiting our website. We hope it gives you a sense of the warmth, ambition and strong community that make Sunnydown such a special place to learn and grow.
We look forward to welcoming you to our school.
Richard Woolley - Headteacher

Our History
Sunnydown School is proud of its rich history, strong sense of community and the unique character that makes our school such a special place to learn and grow.
At the heart of the school is Portley House, a beautiful Victorian building full of history and charm. Built in 1856 for Charles Dingwall, a London wine merchant, the house has stood proudly in Caterham for more than 150 years. There has long been local interest in the building’s connection to the port wine trade, with stories linking it to the founders of Taylor’s Port, adding to the character and heritage of the site.
Originally built as a family home, Portley House became one of the first grand houses developed in Caterham following the arrival of the railway. Many of its original features and period character remain today, giving the school a warm and welcoming atmosphere that is appreciated by students, staff and visitors alike.
The building later became Portley House Boarding Special School and developed a long tradition of residential education and care. Boarding remained an important part of Sunnydown for many years, supporting students from across Surrey and helping young people build independence, friendships and confidence within a caring school community. The residential provision officially closed in 2021 as the school continued to evolve to meet the changing needs of students and families.
Since Sunnydown School moved to the site in 1983, the school has continued to grow and develop while carefully preserving the history and spirit of the building. Over the years, modern classrooms and specialist facilities have been added to support high quality teaching and learning, creating an environment where tradition and innovation sit side by side.
Sunnydown has always been more than just a school building. It is a community built on kindness, respect and positive relationships.
Generations of students have walked through the doors of Portley House, each contributing to the life and story of the school. The warmth, support and sense of belonging felt across the school today remain central to everything we do.
As Sunnydown continues to grow, we remain proud of our past and excited for the future. Our history reminds us of where we have come from, while inspiring us to continue providing outstanding opportunities, care and support for every young person in our community.

Friends of Sunnydown
The Friends of Sunnydown (FoS) is the school’s registered charity and parent and community support group, dedicated to enriching the lives and experiences of the young people at Sunnydown School.
Everyone connected to the school is automatically part of Friends of Sunnydown, including parents, carers, families, staff, governors and members of the wider community. Together, we work to strengthen relationships across the school community while raising valuable funds that directly benefit our students.
FoS supports projects, activities and opportunities that enhance learning, personal development and wellbeing for our young people. Fundraising has helped provide specialist equipment, enrichment activities, sensory and wellbeing spaces, social events and wider life experiences that go beyond what traditional funding can provide.
As a specialist setting supporting young people with communication and interaction needs, Sunnydown places great importance on creating a sense of belonging and community. Friends of Sunnydown plays a vital role in this by organising inclusive events that allow families, students and staff to connect in supportive and understanding environments. Past events have included quiz nights, raffles, family socials, Christmas activities and community fundraising initiatives.
All funds raised are used solely for the benefit of the students and school community, with trustees and volunteers giving their time freely to support the charity’s work.
Friends of Sunnydown is a registered charity (Charity Number 1165806) and continues to welcome the support, ideas and involvement of families, local businesses and the wider community in helping our young people thrive.

Curriculum
At Sunnydown School, we believe that every student deserves an education that inspires confidence, develops character and creates opportunities for a successful future. Guided by our vision of Every Day. Every Lesson. Every Student. A Better Future., our curriculum is designed to provide students with the knowledge, skills and experiences they need to thrive both in school and beyond.
The curriculum at Sunnydown School is ambitious, inclusive and personalised. We recognise that every student arrives with their own strengths, interests and experiences, and our approach ensures that all students are supported to achieve their full potential. Through high quality teaching, strong pastoral care and a culture of high expectations, we create an environment where students feel safe, valued and ready to learn.
Students experience a broad and balanced curriculum that combines academic study with creative, technical, practical and enrichment opportunities. Learning is carefully sequenced to build knowledge over time, enabling students to make meaningful connections between subjects and apply their understanding in a range of contexts.
Explore our Subject Overviews to learn more about what is taught across the curriculum and how knowledge and skills are developed within each subject area.
Building Strong Foundations
The curriculum journey at Sunnydown School begins with a focus on belonging, confidence and engagement. Students are supported to develop positive learning habits, strengthen their literacy and communication skills and build the foundations needed for future success. Through a carefully structured programme of study, students learn to become increasingly independent, resilient and reflective learners.
Pastoral support is woven throughout the curriculum, ensuring that students are able to succeed both academically and personally. Strong relationships, clear routines and high expectations help every student to feel part of the Sunnydown School community.
Find out more about Key Stage 3 and how students develop the knowledge, skills and confidence needed for the next stage of their education.
Preparing for Life Beyond School
As students progress through Sunnydown School, the curriculum becomes increasingly focused on independence, achievement and preparation for adulthood. Students follow a personalised pathway that enables them to gain meaningful qualifications while continuing to develop the personal qualities and practical skills required for life beyond school.
A distinctive feature of the Sunnydown School curriculum is its focus on real-world learning. Through the Friday Curriculum, careers education, enrichment opportunities and community engagement, students apply their learning in meaningful contexts and explore future education, employment and training pathways.
By the time students leave Sunnydown School, they are equipped with the qualifications, character, confidence and life skills needed to move successfully into further education, training or employment.
Find out more about Key Stage 4 and how students are supported to achieve their aspirations and prepare for their future.
At Sunnydown School, our aim is simple: to ensure that every student leaves with the knowledge, skills, character and confidence to lead a happy, successful and fulfilling life.
